body:
Found by the cross-family review of #1427 (Sol), 2026-08-07. VERIFIED as
pre-existing: it is not introduced by that PR.

Both writers of KOSyncProgress implement furthest-wins as read, compare in
Python, mutate, commit -- with no row lock, no optimistic version column, and no
conditional UPDATE against the percentage that was actually observed:

  * update_progress()                  (kosync.py, the KOReader PUT path)
        progress_record = get_progress_record(...)
        if same_device or percentage_float >= progress_record.percentage:
            progress_record.percentage = percentage_float
            ...

  * record_percentage_only_progress()  (kosync.py, added by #1427 for the browser)
        record = get_progress_record(...)
        if percentage < record.percentage: return False
        record.progress = PERCENTAGE_ONLY_LOCATOR
        ...

A competing transaction can change the row between the read and the flush, so
the comparison is made against a value that is no longer current.

Concrete interleaving:

  1. Row holds 50% with a real KOReader xpointer.
  2. Browser request A reads the row at 50% and approves a write of 60%.
  3. KOReader request B reads the same row, approves 70% with a real xpointer,
     and commits.
  4. A flushes its already-approved 60% write.
  5. Final state: 60%, progress = "cwng:percentage".

Two independent losses: stored progress regresses 70 -> 60, contradicting
furthest-wins, and an exact locator is replaced by a percentage-only marker. The
same shape exists between two browser saves and between two devices.

Exposure notes. The app runs gevent WITHOUT monkey.patch_all(), so within a
single worker a handler's DB call does not yield mid-sequence and the window is
small; it is real across workers/processes, and #1427 widens it by adding a
second writer to a row that previously had one.

Why it is filed rather than fixed in #1427: the defect lives in the shared
pattern, and a correct fix (a conditional UPDATE guarded on the observed
percentage, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE where the backend supports it) has to
change update_progress() too. Bolting it onto a PR about the web-reader carrier
would mean changing the long-standing KOReader write path under that PR's
verification rather than its own.

Suggested fix: make the comparison part of the write -- UPDATE ... WHERE
percentage <= :incoming -- and treat rowcount 0 as "someone else was further",
which is already the semantic both callers want.
title: KOSync furthest-wins is an unlocked read-compare-write, so a concurrent push can regress progress
